mac.key: ["running","Mac ↔ apollo, mars's box on Linux (direct 10 GbE, X540)","SM1c-small-onto-mac-confirm"]
mac.text: The Mac, a MacBook Pro with an M1 Max and a Thunderbolt 10 GbE adapter, is wired directly over 10 GbE to a Linux machine called apollo, which is mars's box. The lab is now running a confirmation test of whether the xs-cpp-noatomic build beats xs-cpp by more than 5% on a large transfer job, following up an earlier result with fresh measurement blocks.

mars.text: This pair links neo, a Raspberry Pi 5 with 4 GB of memory and an NVMe drive, to mars, a 12-core Ryzen 9 desktop with 32 GB of memory, over a wired gigabit connection. It is idle right now, with no experiment running.

neo.text: The pair neo and vpsb are joined by a wired link. The experiment is idle, since no runner is currently active and no experiment is set.

neo-ssd.text: neo, a Raspberry Pi 5 with 4 GB of memory and an NVMe drive, is linked to its partner over a local SSD connection. Paused, it asks whether capping neo at 2 CPUs widens xs -a -j4's deficit to rsync -a on cold local copies of real-psample.
